cards.title: Track organic search revenue as the primary SEO KPI
cards.summary: Judge SEO by organic search revenue, not traffic, rankings or vanity blog metrics.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an SEO agency's monthly reporting or deciding whether SEO spend is working for your store.

cards.title: Use a lean SEO tool stack: Semrush, Google Keyword Planner, Screaming Frog
cards.summary: Run ecommerce SEO with three tools: an all-in-one suite, a free keyword planner, and a crawler.
cards.use_when: Choosing or trimming SEO tool subscriptions and setting up keyword and technical research for a store.

cards.title: Build standout content and relationships for free organic links
cards.summary: Earn links via journalist/blogger relationships and standout content, but expect it to be slow and costly relative to paid links.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in digital PR and link-worthy content versus paid link acquisition for a store.

cards.title: Build a keyword strategy combining money pages and backlinks
cards.summary: Combine transactional keyword targeting on collection pages with a small set of quality backlinks to drive organic revenue.
cards.use_when: Planning a quarter of SEO work for a store: which pages to create/optimize and which links to acquire.

cards.title: Technical SEO on Shopify: Audit Order and Purpose
cards.summary: Run a three-step Shopify technical SEO audit (manual, crawl, Search Console) as the foundation before content or link work.
cards.use_when: Before investing in content marketing or link building for your store; when organic rankings are stagnant and you don't know if the technical foundation is broken.

cards.title: Fix Shopify Product URL Duplication (Within-Collection Paths)
cards.summary: Remove the within-collection URL parameter in Shopify theme code so product links always resolve to the canonical /products/ URL.
cards.use_when: When auditing technical SEO on a Shopify store and product URLs appear as /collections/x/products/y when navigated from a collection.

cards.title: Rebuild Shopify Breadcrumbs With a Meta Field After URL Fix
cards.summary: Shopify builds breadcrumbs from the URL path, so fixing product URLs breaks them - store collection links in a breadcrumb meta field and render from that.
cards.use_when: After removing the within_collection parameter (or any time breadcrumbs on product/collection pages disappear or show wrong hierarchy).

cards.title: No-Index Auto-Generated Tag, Vendor, Type, and Utility Pages
cards.summary: Shopify generates thin tag/vendor/type/utility pages that can't be customized, so set them to noindex, follow.
cards.use_when: When the store has many product tags (sizes, colors, skin types) or blog tags, or when GSC shows many thin/duplicate pages indexed.

cards.title: Custom robots.txt on Shopify: Block Low-Value Pages
cards.summary: Create a custom robots.txt in a Shopify template to block crawling of auto-generated, duplicate, and low-value pages.
cards.use_when: After you have set low-value pages to noindex, as defense-in-depth to save crawl budget from duplicate/tag/vendor churn.

cards.title: Manage Variant Duplication: Merge or Canonicalize
cards.summary: Merge low-search-volume variants into one product, or keep them but point canonical tags at the primary product URL.
cards.use_when: When color/size variants each create near-duplicate product listings (e.g., cotton sock green vs cotton sock black) with no distinct descriptions or search volume.

cards.title: Redirect Deleted Products to Preserve Redirect Path and Link Equity
cards.summary: Never let deleted product URLs 404 - 301 redirect them to a related product or collection to keep visitors and link equity.
cards.use_when: Whenever a product is removed or discontinued and was previously live, especially if it received traffic or backlinks.

cards.title: Remove Pages from Shopify Sitemaps Correctly (Avoid the Hidden SEO Trap)
cards.summary: Shopify requires manual sitemap exclusion, and the hidden SEO checkbox also forces noindex, nofollow - use the theme meta tag instead.
cards.use_when: When you canonicalize or want to exclude pages from the sitemap without preventing them from ranking (e.g., variant or parameter pages).

cards.title: Implement Product, Article, and Breadcrumb Structured Data
cards.summary: Verify and enrich schema so products show price, ratings, shipping, and returns in search results, and breadcrumbs show hierarchy.
cards.use_when: When you want rich snippets for product and blog listings, or when auditing technical SEO to ensure schema is valid.

cards.title: Posture Site Speed: Avoid Bloat Rather Than Optimize
cards.summary: Shopify is fast out of the box; site speed work mostly means avoiding heavy themes, oversized images, and unused/unconditional apps.
cards.use_when: When store pages feel slow, mobile conversion lags, or before adding new apps, sliders, or hero assets.

cards.title: Choose Lightweight Themes and Cut Hero/Grid Bloat
cards.summary: Prefer lean themes (Dawn free; Palo Alto paid) and replace sliders, carousels, and oversized grids with simpler components.
cards.use_when: At store build time or when auditing an existing Shopify theme that feels sluggish on mobile.

cards.title: Optimize Image Format and Compression for Speed
cards.summary: Use WebP/JPEG for product images, WebP/PNG for hero text graphics, SVG for logos, and auto-compress with an app.
cards.use_when: When preparing product photography, hero images, logos, or auditing an image-heavy collection page.

cards.title: Lazy Load Offscreen Images on Collection Pages
cards.summary: Delay loading images until they approach the viewport so long product grids don't load every image up front.
cards.use_when: On collection/category pages with many product images (e.g., 36-grid) where only the first rows are visible at load.

cards.title: Audit and Remove Unused App Code from Themes
cards.summary: Uninstalling a Shopify app often leaves its scripts behind in the theme, so sweep with PageSpeed Insights and remove orphan code.
cards.use_when: After uninstalling apps, or when third-party script overhead is flagged on the store.

cards.title: Conditionally Load App Scripts by Page Type
cards.summary: Load each app's scripts only on pages where they're needed instead of sitewide via theme.liquid.
cards.use_when: When review widgets, zoom scripts, custom-option code, or social share buttons load on every page and slow unrelated pages.

cards.title: Minify JavaScript and CSS to Reduce File Size
cards.summary: Strip comments, spacing, and line breaks from JS/CSS to shrink files and speed up loading.
cards.use_when: When PageSpeed or an audit shows unminified JS/CSS asset opportunities on the store.

cards.title: Speed up a Shopify store by minifying CSS/JS
cards.summary: Remove whitespace, line breaks and comments from CSS/JS to cut file size and speed up page load.
cards.use_when: When auditing storefront page speed and deciding whether technical asset optimisation is worth the effort before other work.

cards.title: Async and defer non-essential scripts
cards.summary: Load chat widgets, analytics and tracking scripts asynchronously or deferred so the page renders and becomes interactive sooner.
cards.use_when: When third-party scripts (live chat, analytics, tracking pixels) are blocking rendering and hurting storefront speed.

cards.title: Use resource hints and preload to cut load times
cards.summary: Add preload, prefetch, DNS-prefetch and preconnect link elements in the head to control how and when key resources load.
cards.use_when: When optimising storefront load speed for above-the-fold assets, next-page navigation, or third-party domains like analytics and social buttons.

cards.title: Frame keyword research around customer thought process, not just volume
cards.summary: Keyword research is uncovering the search terms people use when looking for your products, services or information — it maps the customer's thought process.
cards.use_when: When planning which collections, product pages and blog posts to build or optimise for organic search on a Shopify store.

cards.title: Build a topical map instead of a flat keyword list
cards.summary: A topical map is keyword research extended into a roadmap of every topic and page needed to be seen as the authority in your niche.
cards.use_when: When a store has scattered SEO pages and you need a single plan for which collections, subcollections and blog posts should exist.

cards.title: Decide page type by what ranks in positions 1–3
cards.summary: Match your target page type (collection, product, or blog post) to the content type Google already rewards for that keyword.
cards.use_when: When a keyword cluster could plausibly be served by a collection page, a product page or a blog post and you need to choose.

cards.title: Prioritise bottom-of-funnel pages first on Shopify
cards.summary: Start SEO with collection and product pages, because they lead directly to revenue and pay back fastest.
cards.use_when: When deciding what to optimise first across hundreds of existing collection and product pages.

cards.title: One topic per page, many secondary keywords per page
cards.summary: Cluster a primary keyword with its close variants on one page, and split genuinely different topics onto separate pages.
cards.use_when: When mapping keywords to URLs so one page can rank for many terms without competing against your own pages.

cards.title: Assign URL types: collections for options, products for specifics, homepage for breadth
cards.summary: Collection pages capture broad transactional terms, product pages capture highly specific ones, and the homepage targets broad high-level keywords.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether a keyword should live on a collection, a product page, or the homepage.

cards.title: Derive site structure and internal links from the topical map
cards.summary: A clean topical map becomes a site structure of homepage, collections and subcollections that mirrors how search engines expect topics to relate.
cards.use_when: When building or restructuring catalogue hierarchy and internal links for a Shopify store.

cards.title: Spot and fix keyword cannibalisation
cards.summary: Cannibalisation is multiple pages on your site competing for the same keyword, which confuses search engines about which page to rank.
cards.use_when: When a collection, product or blog page isn't ranking as expected and you suspect competing pages on the same store.

cards.title: Expand broad topics into subcollections without creating redundancy
cards.summary: Splitting a broad category into focused subcollections captures more search entry points, but only where each page has a genuinely distinct offer.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether to break a large collection into subcollections or keep it as one page.

cards.title: Stick to your core topic and avoid diluting relevance
cards.summary: Publishing content far outside your topical map dilutes the site's perceived expertise and can cost rankings on core topics.
cards.use_when: When considering a new category, blog theme, or shoulder niche that sits outside your store's existing topic focus.

cards.title: Optimise the main menu for fewer clicks to product
cards.summary: Match main-menu structure to catalogue size: minimal for small stores, direct subcategory access for large, shop-by-x for varied ranges.
cards.use_when: When designing or revising the storefront main navigation to improve usability and crawl efficiency.

cards.title: Make the homepage a hub for high-volume collections
cards.summary: Feature your highest-search-volume collection pages prominently at the top of the homepage to serve users and push backlink equity into money pages.
cards.use_when: When designing homepage layout and choosing which collections to surface first.

cards.title: Handle faceted navigation correctly on Shopify
cards.summary: Default Shopify filter URLs are parameter-based and are not indexed, so keyword-targeted filters need their own dedicated collection pages.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether to add filters to a collection page and whether those filters should rank for anything.

cards.title: Build product grids for both users and crawlers
cards.summary: Avoid JavaScript-loaded product grids, show 36–48 products per page, and put useful product details directly in the grid.
cards.use_when: When setting up or redesigning collection page product grids on a Shopify store.

cards.title: Add breadcrumbs, tag-style links and related products to product pages
cards.summary: Use three internal-link patterns on product pages to strengthen navigation, distribute link equity and aid discovery.
cards.use_when: When auditing product page template and internal linking on a Shopify store.

cards.title: Optimise the three key on-page elements on collection pages
cards.summary: Title tag, URL and H1 are the first elements search engines crawl and the strongest signal of what the page is about.
cards.use_when: When writing or rewriting collection page metadata for a Shopify store.

cards.title: Decide what to do with a page: publish, refresh, or quick-win
cards.summary: Track each mapped topic's publication and performance status so the topical map becomes an actionable worklist rather than a document.
cards.use_when: When turning a completed keyword/topical map into a prioritised production and optimisation queue.

cards.title: Shopify Collection Page Content Stack
cards.summary: Layered content template for collection pages: short description, detailed description, FAQ accordion, featured reviews.
cards.use_when: Building or rewriting a Shopify collection/category page template to rank and convert.

cards.title: Splitting One Shopify Description into Short and Detailed Sections
cards.summary: Technical method to serve a short collection description above and a long one below the product grid using Shopify template code.
cards.use_when: A theme only exposes one collection description field but you need both a short top summary and a long bottom description.

cards.title: Why Add Unique Content to Hundreds of Collection Pages
cards.summary: Strategic rationale for adding human-written content to every collection page: big retailers can't or won't, so it's your ranking opening.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in content for each collection page when you have many collections.

cards.title: Product Detail Info and Faceted Navigation on Collection Pages
cards.summary: Add specification-style product details and filtering directly on collection pages to improve UX and relevance.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a collection page for user experience and adding unique content, especially with many SKUs.

cards.title: FAQ Accordions on Collection and Product Pages
cards.summary: Add FAQ accordions sourced from People Also Ask, with lightweight code and structured data.
cards.use_when: Adding an FAQ section to collection or product pages to answer pre-purchase questions and earn rich results.

cards.title: Featured Reviews on Collection Pages
cards.summary: Manually place 3 keyword-rich customer reviews at the bottom of collection pages for both conversion and SEO.
cards.use_when: Improving collection page conversion and adding unique content without a heavy review app.

cards.title: Deciding Whether to Rank a Product Page vs a Collection Page
cards.summary: Use SERP inspection of the target term to decide whether to build a product page or a collection page.
cards.use_when: Allocating SEO effort to either a product page or a collection page for a specific keyword.

cards.title: Evaluating Search Volume Before Investing in Product Page SEO
cards.summary: Decide whether to optimize, or noindex, product pages based on whether their (often invented) names actually get searched.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend SEO effort across a large product catalog with many custom-named SKUs.

cards.title: Handling Discontinued and Out-of-Stock Product Pages
cards.summary: Never delete ranking discontinued/out-of-stock product pages — keep them live with replacement CTAs or restock notifications.
cards.use_when: Managing product pages for items that are discontinued or temporarily out of stock.

cards.title: Product Page Content Template for Shopify SEO
cards.summary: Structured product page layout: short description, features/benefits, spec table, detailed description, FAQ, reviews, images.
cards.use_when: Rebuilding a product page template for SEO and conversion on Shopify.

cards.title: Product Page Images, Alt Text, and XML Sitemap
cards.summary: Image SEO for product pages: descriptive filenames, alt text, WebP/JPEG, compression, lazy loading, sitemap inclusion.
cards.use_when: Optimizing images on product pages to improve conversion and SEO, and ensuring images are indexable.

cards.title: Product Page Structured Data: Product, Review, FAQ, Breadcrumb
cards.summary: The four schema types product pages should use, and why rich snippets increase CTR.
cards.use_when: Adding or verifying structured data on product pages to earn rich snippets.

cards.title: Breadcrumbs, Tag-Style Category Links, and Related Product Modules
cards.summary: On-page navigation elements that support internal linking and user navigation on product pages.
cards.use_when: Improving product page navigation, internal linking, and discoverability on Shopify.

cards.title: When a Shopify Store Needs a Blog
cards.summary: Blog content ranks informational terms and, more importantly, supports collection page rankings via internal linking and topical authority.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in a blog and how much to prioritize it for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Optimizing Blog Post Titles, H1, URL, and Meta Description
cards.summary: The three on-page SEO elements for blogs plus the meta description, and where to set them in Shopify.
cards.use_when: Creating or auditing a Shopify blog post for on-page SEO.

cards.title: Writing Blog Content That Beats What Ranks
cards.summary: Match or exceed the structure and comprehensiveness of the pages currently ranking for your target term.
cards.use_when: Drafting a blog post meant to rank for a specific informational keyword.

cards.title: Embedding Product CTAs and Internal Links in Blog Posts
cards.summary: Place relevant product CTAs and contextual internal links to convert blog readers and pass authority to shopping pages.
cards.use_when: Monetizing blog traffic and using blog posts to strengthen product/collection pages.

cards.title: Building Topical Authority One Cluster at a Time
cards.summary: Fully cover a single topic cluster before expanding to adjacent topics so search engines recognize your expertise.
cards.use_when: Planning blog/content production across topics for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: What Ecommerce Link Building Is and Why It Matters
cards.summary: Backlinks act as votes of confidence; competitive keywords are won by sites with hundreds or thousands of backlinks.
cards.use_when: Planning off-page SEO for a Shopify or ecommerce brand.

cards.title: Foundational Links for a New Ecommerce Site
cards.summary: Basic directory and social links establish that your store exists and signal what it's about.
cards.use_when: Onboarding a new ecommerce site with no backlink profile.

cards.title: Map the five link-building types to an ecommerce backlink mix
cards.summary: Foundational, guest post, niche edit, expert-quote, linkable-asset and digital-PR links each play a different role in a Shopify store's off-page profile.
cards.use_when: Planning a quarterly off-page SEO plan for a store and deciding where to spend outreach time and budget.

cards.title: Judge a backlink's quality before pursuing it
cards.summary: Six factors — follow status, anchor text, topical relevance, authority metrics, link target page and site quality — determine whether a backlink helps or hurts your store.
cards.use_when: Vetting a prospect site or an inbound link offer before you write a guest post, accept a placement or pay a fee.

cards.title: Run a link-gap analysis and set a monthly link target
cards.summary: Compare your filtered dofollow referring-domain count against SEO competitors to derive a concrete monthly backlink goal.
cards.use_when: Setting link-building targets for a store and deciding how many placements per month to buy or earn.

cards.title: Screen spam links with a five-point checklist
cards.summary: Before accepting or paying for a placement, verify the site is real, topically relevant, has organic traffic and has quality backlinks of its own.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a paid link offer, an inbound guest-post pitch or an email offering backlinks for a store.

cards.title: Build foundational links and citations as the base layer
cards.summary: Set up social profiles, directory listings and Web 2.0 pages so search engines can identify your store as a real entity before you pursue editorial links.
cards.use_when: Launching a new store or a new brand with no backlink profile, before starting guest posting or outreach.

cards.title: Prioritize low-hanging-fruit collection pages for links
cards.summary: Use Semrush's organic research to find pages ranking in positions 4–10, then send links there because they are closest to converting rankings into revenue.
cards.use_when: Choosing which collection or category pages to build links to this month on a store.

cards.title: Prospect link targets by scraping competitors' guest-post backlinks
cards.summary: Identify true SEO competitors, scrape their placement-type backlinks in Semrush, then filter the export to reachable, healthy, relevant sites.
cards.use_when: Building an outreach prospect list for a store's guest posting and niche edit campaign.

cards.title: Find contact details for link prospects
cards.summary: Use email-finding tools for speed, or fall back to manual site inspection, personal emails and contact forms.
cards.use_when: Turning a filtered prospect list into a sendable outreach list for guest posts or niche edits.

cards.title: Write outreach subject lines and bodies that get opened and answered
cards.summary: Personalize subject lines with curiosity, humor or a question, and keep the body short, specific and clear about wanting a dofollow guest post.
cards.use_when: Drafting the first outreach email to a blog or site owner to request a guest post placement.

cards.title: Warm Up Cold Outreach Sending Accounts Before Guest Post Pitching
cards.summary: Set up cold email sending accounts for guest post outreach by warming them up and ramping volume slowly to stay out of spam filters.
cards.use_when: Preparing the email sending infrastructure for a link-building or blogger-outreach campaign on behalf of an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Make Guest Post Pitches Unique Instead of Reusing a Template
cards.summary: Generic outreach templates get ignored, so tailor each pitch to the specific site's niche and audience to beat the template-using majority.
cards.use_when: Writing the outreach email to a blog or site you want to earn a guest post or link from.

cards.title: Close and Negotiate the Guest Post Link, Then Run Final Vetting
cards.summary: Structure the back half of an outreach conversation — vet the site, negotiate terms, and always drive toward securing the link.
cards.use_when: Replying to a positive outreach response and deciding whether and at what price to place a guest post or link on that site.

cards.title: Write a Guest Post That Fits the Host Site's Audience
cards.summary: Craft guest post content around the host blog's readers — not your store's customers — so the post reads as genuinely valuable and earns the link.
cards.use_when: Writing a guest post for a partner blog (e.g., an interior design site) that will link back to one of your store's pages, such as a product collection.

cards.title: Place Guest Post Anchors Naturally and Near the Top
cards.summary: Embed the backlink anchor inside a relevant sentence near the top of the post rather than isolating it on an awkward 'check us out' line.
cards.use_when: Adding the link back to your store's collection or product page while writing a guest post.

cards.title: Diversify Anchor Text and Mirror Competitor Backlink Profiles
cards.summary: Use mostly partial-match, URL, brand, and miscellaneous anchors rather than exact matches, and calibrate the mix by studying your top competitors' backlink profiles.
cards.use_when: Deciding what anchor text to use when placing guest posts or link inserts to a specific store page.

cards.title: Run Final Checks After a Guest Post Goes Live
cards.summary: Verify the live link meets your requirements before counting it as a success.
cards.use_when: After a host publishes your guest post, to confirm the link is correct and valuable.

cards.title: Evaluate relevant link inserts without assuming faster rankings
cards.summary: Add a link to an existing, already-indexed page on a relevant site to get faster SEO impact than a brand-new guest post.
cards.use_when: Choosing between building a new guest post or paying to insert a link on an existing relevant page on a partner site.

cards.title: Pitch ecommerce expertise to journalist sourcing requests
cards.summary: Respond to journalists' source queries on Connectively (formerly HARO) to earn media backlinks and brand visibility for your store.
cards.use_when: Looking to earn high-authority, low-cost backlinks for a store by being quoted as an expert in your niche.

cards.title: Pitch ecommerce expertise to journalist sourcing requests
cards.summary: Make your expert answers easy to read and genuinely expert so journalists pick your quote and link to your store.
cards.use_when: Writing an answer to a journalist's source query on Connectively/HARO for your ecommerce niche.

cards.title: Pitch ecommerce expertise to journalist sourcing requests
cards.summary: Log every query you answer so you can measure conversion to links and decide whether to scale the strategy.
cards.use_when: Running an ongoing HARO/Connectively effort and deciding whether to invest more time or team members.
